faq.a: No, ITR-1 (Sahaj) is exclusively for Resident Individuals. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are not eligible to file ITR-1 and typically need to file ITR-2.

faq.q: What if my income exceeds ₹50 lakhs?
faq.a: If your total income for the financial year exceeds ₹50 lakhs, you are not eligible to file ITR-1. You would generally need to file ITR-2 or ITR-3, depending on your income sources.

faq.q: Can I file ITR-1 if I have a capital gain?
faq.a: No, individuals with any income from capital gains (short-term or long-term, from any asset) are not eligible to file ITR-1. They must file ITR-2.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to e-verify ITR-1?
faq.a: Yes, it is mandatory to verify your ITR-1 after submission. E-verification is the quickest and most preferred method, using Aadhaar OTP, Net Banking, or Demat account. Without verification, your ITR is considered invalid.

faq.q: What is the due date for filing ITR-1 for AY 2026-27?
faq.a: For most individual taxpayers not requiring an audit, the due date for filing ITR for Assessment Year 2026-27 (Financial Year 2025-26) is typically July 31, 2026. Please always refer to the official Income Tax Department notifications for any specific changes or extensions.

faq.q: Can I file ITR-1 if I own two self-occupied properties?
faq.a: No, if you own more than one house property, even if both are self-occupied, you are not eligible to file ITR-1. ITR-1 is specifically for individuals with income from *one* house property. In such a scenario, you would generally need to file ITR-2.
